::: {.why}
Regression on raw forward return, classification on its sign, and ranking within the cross-section are three different problems with three different loss functions, and picking one by habit throws away the choice.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State what each of the three label types optimises and which one matches how you actually trade.
- Report the same model's performance under all three labels, evaluated on a common metric.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Fit all three and evaluate them on the same footing: convert each model's output into a portfolio through the same score-to-weight map, and report information ratio rather than the model's native metric. A classifier with a great AUC and a poor information ratio is the normal outcome and this is where you see it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Say what the fixed-horizon label assumes: that the return over a fixed window is what you care about, regardless of the path. Name two situations where that is false, which are a stop loss and any position you would have exited early, and note that tomorrow's method addresses exactly this.
:::
:::
